ENHS 223.description: Introduction to global environmental health, with a focus on toxic pollution and disease burden in developing countries. Investigation of international treaties, corresponding environmental pollution processes, and human health effects.
ENHS 223.subject: ENHS
ENHS 223.title: Introduction to Global Environmental Health

ENHS 321.description: A survey of pollution (chemical, biological, physical) effects on environmental quality and public health with emphases on how each pollutant class behaves and affects individual and community health over acute to chronic exposure periods.
ENHS 321.subject: ENHS
ENHS 321.title: Environmental Pollution and Health

ENHS 323.description: Concerns in global environmental health, with a focus on toxic pollution and disease burden in developing countries. Investigation of international treaties, corresponding environmental pollution processes, and human health effects.
ENHS 323.subject: ENHS
ENHS 323.title: Global Environmental Health

ENHS 324.description: Role of the built environment and environmental toxins in the development and progression of obesity and metabolic syndrome from a public health perspective.
ENHS 324.subject: ENHS
ENHS 324.title: Environment and Obesity

ENHS 415.description: Introduction to emergency preparedness and response in relation to environmental and public health. Historical context for the emergence of public health emergency preparedness and demonstration of articulation with community response partner agencies in the post-COVID era.
ENHS 415.subject: ENHS
ENHS 415.title: Disasters and Public Health Emergency Management

ENHS 450.description: Public health microbiology and the intersection between microbial disease, the environment, and health, with a particular focus on critical public health issues in the 21st century.
ENHS 450.subject: ENHS
ENHS 450.title: Introduction to Public Health Microbiology

ENHS 490.description: Enrollment and topic to be approved in advance by advisor and instructor. May be repeated.
ENHS 490.subject: ENHS
ENHS 490.title: Independent Study

ENHS 492.description: Issues and emerging themes in environmental health. May be repeated for a total of 9 credit hours as content varies by title.
ENHS 492.subject: ENHS
ENHS 492.title: Special Topics in Environmental Health Sciences

ENHS 515.description: Introduction to emergency preparedness and response in relation to environmental and public health. Historical context for the emergence of public health emergency preparedness and demonstration of articulation with community response partner agencies in the post-COVID era.
ENHS 515.subject: ENHS
ENHS 515.title: Disasters and Public Health Emergency Management

ENHS 555.description: A detailed exploration of the impacts of climate change on human health and well-being.
ENHS 555.subject: ENHS
ENHS 555.title: Climate Change Impacts on Human Health

ENHS 575.description: A study of national, community, and organizational multi-hazard resilience and risk management framed in the public and environmental health contexts.
ENHS 575.subject: ENHS
ENHS 575.title: Public Health and Community Disaster Resilience

ENHS 585.description: A study in the intersection of public health and crisis leadership to develop the knowledge and skills needed to effectively respond to and recover from emergencies and disasters.
ENHS 585.subject: ENHS
ENHS 585.title: Crisis Leadership for the Public Health Professional

ENHS 592.description: Emerging issues and topics concerning environmental health. May be repeated as content varies by title up to a total of 9 credit hours.
ENHS 592.subject: ENHS
ENHS 592.title: Advanced Special Topics in Environmental Health

ENHS 625.description: Advanced study of infectious diseases caused by fungi. Etiology, symptoms, and treatment of fungi related illnesses.
ENHS 625.subject: ENHS
ENHS 625.title: Medical Mycology

ENHS 660.description: Environmental health sciences presenting the earth as a complex system in which people, plants, animals, and non-living physical-chemical components interact.
ENHS 660.subject: ENHS
ENHS 660.title: Concepts of Environmental Health Science

ENHS 661.description: Parasites of biological, economic, and public health importance. Three lecture and three laboratory hours per week.
ENHS 661.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: 300 level Biology course or equivalent.
ENHS 661.subject: ENHS
ENHS 661.title: Parasitology

ENHS 662.description: Analysis, planning, and implementation of programs to protect workers’ health in industry; legislative and regulatory background.
ENHS 662.subject: ENHS
ENHS 662.title: Industrial Health Programs

ENHS 664.description: State of the art molecular techniques that elucidate mechanisms of environmental contaminants in model systems.
ENHS 664.subject: ENHS
ENHS 664.title: Environmental Genomics

ENHS 665.description: Effect of bacterial biofilm process on many diverse areas. Recognition, prevention, and control of biofilm-related problems in the environment, health care, industry, and engineering.
ENHS 665.subject: ENHS
ENHS 665.title: Biofilms in Environmental Health and Disease

ENHS 666.description: Trace metal(loid)s, their fate and transport in the environment and their potential impacts on human health.
ENHS 666.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: BIOL 101 or BIOL 110; CHEM 101 and CHEM 102, or equivalent.
ENHS 666.subject: ENHS
ENHS 666.title: Metals and Human Health

ENHS 670.description: Overview of environmental pollutants and their impact on human health; case studies of environmental catastrophes; principles of ecotoxicology; air, water, and land pollution associated with neurotoxicity, toxicology, and carcinogenesis.
ENHS 670.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: BIOL 101 or BIOL 110; CHEM 101 and CHEM 102.
ENHS 670.subject: ENHS
ENHS 670.title: Environmental Pollutants and Human Health

ENHS 671.description: A receptor-oriented approach for assessing human exposure to environmental contaminants by inhalation, dermal and ingestion routes. Covers methods for estimating exposures to protect health and well-being, to relate adverse effects to exposures, and to comply with regulations and guidelines.
ENHS 671.subject: ENHS
ENHS 671.title: From Air to Alveoli: Exposure Science

ENHS 675.description: Ecological theories as the basis for environmental change and the (re)emergence of infectious agents that ultimately impact human and ecosystem health.
ENHS 675.subject: ENHS
ENHS 675.title: Infectious Disease Ecology

ENHS 681.description: Introduction to ergonomics: hazards identification and analysis; solution design and implementation; human musculoskeletal characteristics, injuries; effects of work on performance, safety, and health. Application to manufacturing and office environments.
ENHS 681.subject: ENHS
ENHS 681.title: Occupational Ergonomics I

ENHS 715.description: Introduction to emergency preparedness and response in relation to environmental and public health. Historical context for the emergence of public health emergency preparedness and demonstration of articulation with community response partner agencies in the post-COVID era.
ENHS 715.subject: ENHS
ENHS 715.title: Disasters and Public Health Emergency Management I

ENHS 716.description: The Disasters and Public Health Emergency Management II companion course is designed for public health practitioners regardless of expertise and particular discipline who must be aware of the emergency management functions relating to public health. The course is designed to familiarize students with the fundamental knowledge needed to address natural and man-made disasters and to follow up where the companion course left off with a specific focus on environmental disasters.
ENHS 716.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: B or better in ENHS 715.
ENHS 716.subject: ENHS
ENHS 716.title: Disasters and Public Health Emergency Management II

ENHS 740.description: Fundamental principles of environmental nanoscience: unique properties of nanomaterials, syntheses and characterization of nanomaterials, and key processes determining their environmental fate and behavior of nanomaterials.
ENHS 740.subject: ENHS
ENHS 740.title: Environmental Nanoscience

ENHS 750.description: Synthesis of foundational and ENHS MPH competencies in preparing a high quality grant proposal to address a public health issue.
ENHS 750.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in PUBH 724, PUBH 725, PUBH 726, PUBH 730, PUBH 735, ENHS 660, ENHS 771, and ENHS 775 .
ENHS 750.subject: ENHS
ENHS 750.title: MPH Integrated Learning Experience (ILE)

ENHS 755.description: Explores the intersection between conservation and environmental health with a particular focus on coastal and marine case studies.
ENHS 755.subject: ENHS
ENHS 755.title: Marine Conservation and Environmental Health

ENHS 760.description: Chemical and physical aspects of air pollution and their regulatory problems. An examination of air pollution sources; physical and chemical processes affecting pollutants after emission; pollutants and their effects and the ultimate fate of pollutants. Attention is also given to the legal, administrative, and technical aspects of air pollution control.
ENHS 760.subject: ENHS
ENHS 760.title: Fundamentals of Air Pollution

ENHS 761.description: Lethal and sublethal effects of environmental stressors on organisms living in the water column and in sediments of aquatic systems. Practical techniques of aquatic toxicology, risk assessment and modeling.
ENHS 761.subject: ENHS
ENHS 761.title: Ecotoxicology of Aquatic Systems

ENHS 762.description: Industrial hygiene, including health effects, occupational health standards, and the evaluation and control of occupational health hazards.
ENHS 762.subject: ENHS
ENHS 762.title: Fundamentals of Industrial Hygiene

ENHS 763.description: Emphasizes the medical aspects of exposure to hazardous materials, accidents, and mental and physical stresses on the job. Clinical spectrum of occupational illness with some emphasis on industrial toxicology.
ENHS 763.subject: ENHS
ENHS 763.title: Medical Aspects of Occupational Health

ENHS 764.description: Fate, transformation, and behavior of pollutants in the atmosphere. Exposure and human health impacts of atmospheric particles.
ENHS 764.subject: ENHS
ENHS 764.title: Principles, Methods, and Issues in Air Quality

ENHS 765.description: Current and prospective research associated with the multi-disciplinary areas of environmental health sciences. Critical evaluation of scientific research, and technical writing and oral presentations.
ENHS 765.subject: ENHS
ENHS 765.title: Applied Research in the Environmental Health Sciences

ENHS 766.description: The quantitative application of principles of basic physical, biological, and geochemical principles in assessing and solving environmental problems in lakes, streams, and wetlands. Emphasis on watershed-water quality interactions, trophic state analyses, wasteload impact prediction, toxic chemical fate and transport, wetland values, and classification.
ENHS 766.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: ENHS 660, pre-calculus math, general ecology.
ENHS 766.subject: ENHS
ENHS 766.title: Applied Aquatic Sciences

ENHS 766L.description: Sampling and analysis of the interacting parameters used in assessing water quality and the functioning of aquatic systems.
ENHS 766L.subject: ENHS
ENHS 766L.title: Applied Aquatic Sciences Laboratory

ENHS 767.description: Concepts in systems ecology and ecological modeling. Emphasis on the use of models and computer simulations in examining environmental interactions, predicting environmental impact, and facilitating the process of environmental planning. Lab practice in model development and computer simulation analysis.
ENHS 767.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: MATH 111 or equivalent, ecology, ENHS 660.
ENHS 767.subject: ENHS
ENHS 767.title: Ecological Modeling and Environmental Planning

ENHS 768.description: Control of chemical and physical hazards in the occupational environment. Course covers principles and design of health protection systems such as ventilation systems, collection mechanisms, control of physical factors (excluding radioactivity).
ENHS 768.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: college math and ENHS 762 or consent of instructor.
ENHS 768.subject: ENHS
ENHS 768.title: Industrial Ventilation and Hazard Control

ENHS 769.description: Designing, implementing, and analyzing environmental exposures in the field; error analysis; computation of the value of improved information; hazard identification; dose-response evaluation; and risk characterization.
ENHS 769.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: MATH 141, CHEM 111 and CHEM 112, and BIOS 700 or STAT 701.
ENHS 769.subject: ENHS
ENHS 769.title: Exposure and Risk Assessment

ENHS 770.description: Microbial processes which alter the fate, bioavailability, and toxicity of environmental pollutants: biotransformations of metals and organic pollutants; resistance mechanisms and roles of microbial biofilms in toxin transfer.
ENHS 770.subject: ENHS
ENHS 770.title: Microbial Processes and Pollution

ENHS 771.description: Environmental Health Sciences Seminar is a one credit course that provides the opportunity for graduate students within the department and other related departments/programs to enhance and broaden their knowledge in environmental health by exploring current research and case studies.
ENHS 771.subject: ENHS
ENHS 771.title: Environmental Health Sciences Seminar

ENHS 772.description: Focuses on history, theory, and practice of predicting, managing, and communicating potential human health and environmental risks of hazardous chemicals. Reviews fundamental components and explores uncertainties, probabilistic approaches, and ‘real-world’ challenges of risk analysis.
ENHS 772.subject: ENHS
ENHS 772.title: Human and Ecological Risk Assessment

ENHS 773.description: Physics of radiation and associated health hazards; hazard evaluation and measurements; radiation content and protection of the individual. Course covers ionizing radiation, ultraviolet, microwave, lasers, R.F. field, and ultra-sound.
ENHS 773.subject: ENHS
ENHS 773.title: Radiation Health Physics

ENHS 774.description: A study of biological interactions and transformation of environmental toxicants at the cellular and subcellular levels, and assessment of cellular damage as it relates to health hazards and risks. Topics to include: environmental toxicants; exposure measurements; factors affecting interactions and toxicity; metabolism of xenobiotics: types and levels of effects and interactions; and human health risks.
ENHS 774.subject: ENHS
ENHS 774.title: Risk Assessment and Interactions of Environmental Toxicants

ENHS 775.description: Review of ecological principles as applied to environmental impact assessment. Study of the mandates of the National Environmental Policy Act of 1969. Analysis of several impact assessment methodologies.
ENHS 775.subject: ENHS
ENHS 775.title: Resource Management and Environmental Impact Assessment

ENHS 776.description: Introduction to environmental planning. Survey of major federal environmental legislation. Review of processes and techniques of environmental planning including zoning, permits, management plans, assessments, and evaluation methods. Case studies of significant environmental projects.
ENHS 776.subject: ENHS
ENHS 776.title: Environmental Regulation and Planning

ENHS 777.description: Fundamentals on the biological effects of ionizing radiation on living systems, especially man; basic biological mechanisms which bring about somatic and genetic effects.
ENHS 777.subject: ENHS
ENHS 777.title: Radiation Biology

ENHS 778.description: Sources, sinks, transport, and transformation of air pollutants. Health effects that occur directly or by intermediate transport. Current monitoring methods and modeling techniques for air pollution.
ENHS 778.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: one year each of general chemistry and physics.
ENHS 778.subject: ENHS
ENHS 778.title: Air Pollution Monitoring and Modeling

ENHS 779.description: Lecture and laboratory investigations concerning sublethal and lethal physiological responses of aquatic organisms to a variety of environmental pollutants. Stresses the in-depth understanding of the effects of: bacterial and thermal pollution, pesticides/herbicides, industrial chemicals, hazardous materials, and petroleum hydrocarbons on different physiological mechanisms.
ENHS 779.subject: ENHS
ENHS 779.title: Applied Environmental Physiology

ENHS 780.description: A critical review of recent advances and case histories in the formulation and use of ecological/ environmental models. Ecosystems analysis and environmental planning.
ENHS 780.subject: ENHS
ENHS 780.title: Advanced Seminar in Environmental Modeling

ENHS 781.description: Literature reviews and applications in evaluation of hazards and design of ergonomic interventions including human factors in information processing, design of displays and controls, vibration, macroergonomics, fatigue, and shiftwork.
ENHS 781.subject: ENHS
ENHS 781.title: Occupational Ergonomics II

ENHS 787.description: Physical and chemical principles of environmental qualitative and quantitative analysis with emphasis on atmospheric, aquatic, and terrestrial samples. Includes use and limitations of instrumental techniques, sampling strategies, data management and reduction, and quality assurance programs.
ENHS 787.subject: ENHS
ENHS 787.title: Analytical Concepts for Environmental Health Sciences

ENHS 788.description: Chemical and physical principles of multimedia contaminant transport, environmental effects of hazardous materials, statutes and regulations classification, treatment and disposal of hazardous materials.
ENHS 788.subject: ENHS
ENHS 788.title: Concepts of Hazardous Materials Management I

ENHS 789.description: Chemical and physical properties of hazardous materials; use and storage; disposal options; transportation requirements; site safety considerations; management systems involving hazardous materials.
ENHS 789.subject: ENHS
ENHS 789.title: Concepts of Hazardous Materials Management II

ENHS 793.description: Content varies by title. Course may be repeated for a total of 6 credit hours.
ENHS 793.subject: ENHS
ENHS 793.title: Special Topics in Environmental Health Sciences

ENHS 794.description: The course is intended to develop theoretical and practical knowledge in environmental science research. The learning formats will permit focus on areas of interest as a means to develop the research skills for later projects. Guided by focus, students may work in the laboratory, field, and/or use existing data.
ENHS 794.subject: ENHS
ENHS 794.title: Introduction to Environmental Science Research

ENHS 795.description: Problems associated with coastal population growth and development. Emphasis is on the working group approach to ameliorating impacts on ecosystem and human health.
ENHS 795.subject: ENHS
ENHS 795.title: Issues in Coastal Environmental Health

ENHS 796.description: Laboratory based course aimed at developing theoretical and practical knowledge in regards to nanoscience in toxicology and in the environment. Students will perform nanoparticle syntheses, characterization, fate and behavior studies or toxicology exposures. Learning formats will permit focus on areas of interest aimed at developing research skills.
ENHS 796.subject: ENHS
ENHS 796.title: Introduction to Nanoanalytics

ENHS 797.description: Global environmental health with a focus on food security in developing nations, including crop responses to warming, soil changes, more variable precipitation inputs and expanding geographical range of pests.
ENHS 797.subject: ENHS
ENHS 797.title: Global Environmental Health and Food Security

ENHS 798.description: Performance of a limited work or service project in a public need setting, pursuit of planned learning objectives related to previously identified aspects of the student’s chosen role. Self-monitoring and regular seminars focusing on learning accomplishments.
ENHS 798.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: 9-10 hours of specified courses including BIOS 700, EPID 700.
ENHS 798.subject: ENHS
ENHS 798.title: Public Health Practice

ENHS 859.description: This course is intended for Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) graduate students to enhance their knowledge of research methods and approaches to address contemporary environmental health sciences issues. The learning formats will allow examination and focus on areas of scientific inquiry and interest as a means to develop the research skills for subsequent research. Guided by focus and instructor guidance through lecture and individual mentoring, students may conduct preliminary pilot research in the laboratory, field, and/or from a review of existing scientific data. Development of the basic scientific background literature review and formulation of the research questions to be tested as part of the final dissertation will be the focus of this research. Further development and enhancement of technical writing, oral communication and research translation skills will be gained.
ENHS 859.subject: ENHS
ENHS 859.title: Advanced Research Approaches and Applications in Environmental Health Sciences

ENHS 860.description: Technical coverage relevant to a practical evaluation of radiation sources and contaminants in the environment.
ENHS 860.subject: ENHS
ENHS 860.title: Environmental Radiation Surveillance

ENHS 861.description: Physical and chemical principles applied to the behavior and properties of particles suspended in air. Course covers motion under applied forces, electrical properties, diffusion, removal from gas, cloud dynamics, and optical properties.
ENHS 861.subject: ENHS
ENHS 861.title: Aerosol Science

ENHS 862.description: Discussion and/or laboratory participation involving techniques used in multidisciplinary research areas of environmental health sciences that have not been covered by other courses. May be repeated for credit on different topics.
ENHS 862.subject: ENHS
ENHS 862.title: Special Research Topics in Environmental Health Sciences

ENHS 863.description: Detailed analyses of techniques, especially computer simulation modeling, used in environmental assessment and planning. Emphasis will be on the prediction of the ecological effects of development projects. Students will collectively construct a simulation model for the purpose of environmental assessment.
ENHS 863.subject: ENHS
ENHS 863.title: Advanced Topics in Environmental Planning

ENHS 864.description: This course is intended for Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) graduate students to enhance their knowledge of current research approaches and to address contemporary environmental health sciences issues. The learning format will allow students to examine the potential of current research and be exposed to a variety of environmental health sciences issues that will enable students to develop foundational research knowledge needed for their subsequent dissertations. In ENHS 864, students will be presented with a variety of environmental health sciences research and topics in a survey fashion. Students will be presented with lectures covering various scientific research including primary laboratory and field research as well as secondary research analyzing existing scientific data. Students will then select a scientific topic in Environmental Health Sciences to lead a class discussion in which they will also provide an overview of the research and will critically examine the strengths and weaknesses of the research methods, data analysis, results, discussions and conclusions. The final section of the course will include lectures on research translation and how to develop a Community Engagement component to their research. This will entail essentially communication elements with the public to develop prevention/restoration strategies that will improve human and/or ecosystem health and well-being.
ENHS 864.subject: ENHS
ENHS 864.title: Survey in Multi-Disciplinary Research of Environmental Health Sciences

ENHS 865.description: A comprehensive overview of community-based approaches for environmental public health assessment. Emphasis of this course is placed on introducing the rapidly evolving field of wastewater-based epidemiology (WBE) where wastewater-derived measurements of human health biomarkers indicative of various aspects of human and environmental health (infectious disease, pollutant exposures, nutritional status, etc.) offer as an inclusive and minimally invasive source of information in support a precision-based model for community-level environmental public health assessment.
ENHS 865.subject: ENHS
ENHS 865.title: Community-Based Approaches for Precision Environmental Public Health Assessment

ENHS 880.description: Overview of skills and standards, including ethics and research preparation, for Environmental Health Sciences doctoral students.
ENHS 880.subject: ENHS
ENHS 880.title: Ethics Research Prep

ENHS 890.description: Directed research on a topic to be developed by doctoral student and instructor. May be repeated.
ENHS 890.subject: ENHS
ENHS 890.title: Independent Study

ENHS 899.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: one full year (18 hrs) of graduate study beyond the master’s level.
ENHS 899.subject: ENHS
ENHS 899.title: Dissertation Preparation
